text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov will not participate at the meeting of foreign ministers of the Council of Baltic Sea Countries which will take place on July 2-3 in Riga. Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Avdeyev will represent Russia at this meeting.
- President Guntis Ulmanis opened the third seminar organised by the United Nations Development Programme on human rights oraganisations.
- The country's biggest daily is late today because of printing problems.
- A professional training centre for the unemployed was opened in Riga. It will be able to train and retrain about 9,000 people per year.
- The first meeting of the intergovernmental commission of Latvia and Belorussia on the demarcation of the border between two states took place in Daugavpils. The next meeting is due in mid-July.
- In the first quarter of 1997 tforestry product exports increased to 79.233 million lats compared to 48.023 million lats (FOB prices) in the same period last year 1996.
- Latvian Shipping negotiates a swap with Latvenergo of its debts, worth $37.35 million. Both companies are currently in the privatisation process.
- Riga Shipyard received its first order from Norway to build several 35-metre fishing-boats - each worth 450,000 lats.
- The budget for the Soros Foundation's Latvian branch in 1996 was more than $4.5 million, four million of which was spent on project financing.
